message.content:
Based on the visual comparison of the two EMI Calculator designs:

**(1) Most Prominent Element**
*   **Old Design:** The **"Loan Parameters" input section** (the dark blue card containing the sliders for Loan Amount, Interest Rate, and Tenure) dominates the upper two-thirds of the screen. It is visually heavy and takes up the most space.
*   **New Design:** The **Monthly EMI value (₹1,26,660)** is the most prominent element. It is displayed in a very large, bold font at the very top of the content area, making it impossible to miss immediately upon opening the page.

**(2) Position of Monthly EMI Value**
*   **Old Design:** Positioned at the **bottom** of the screen, below all the input sliders and quick preset buttons. A user must scroll down past the inputs to see it.
*   **New Design:** Positioned at the **top** of the main content area, directly under the introductory text. It is the first piece of data presented to the user.

**(3) Is the new design visibly different?**
**Yes, extremely.** This is a complete structural overhaul:
*   **Layout Inversion:** The old design follows an "Input → Output" flow (top-to-bottom), while the new design uses an "Output → Input/Details" flow (results-first).
*   **Visual Hierarchy:** The old design buries the result; the new design elevates it.
*   **Added Elements:** The new design introduces a **donut chart** ("EMI Breakup"), a **bar chart** ("Yearly Principal vs Interest"), and action buttons (**Download Excel/PDF**), which were absent in the old version.
*   **Color & Space:** The heavy dark blue input block in the old design is replaced by a lighter, more open layout with distinct white cards for different sections.

**(4) Which design is better for instant EMI knowledge?**
The **NEW design** is significantly better for a user who wants to know their EMI instantly.

*   **Reasoning:** Mobile users often have short attention spans and want immediate gratification. By placing the large **₹1,26,660 figure at the top**, the new design provides the answer within a split second of loading, without requiring any scrolling or interaction. 
*   **Contrast:** In the old design, the user is forced to interact with (or at least look at) the input parameters first and then scroll down to find the result. The "answer" was hidden at the bottom of the page, which is poor UX for a calculator tool where the primary goal is getting a specific number quickly.
